step1-1: Plug your ESP into a USB port. We’re putting WLED
step1-2: on it. No turning back after this.
step2: Hit “Install.” Pick the right COM port. Get it wrong, and this whole thing falls apart.
serialHelp1: Could be you’re missing the drivers for your board. Happens to the best of us.
serialHelp2: Here’s the drivers for the usual suspects in ESP boards:
serialHelp3: Make sure that cable actually moves data. A charger cable’s a dead end dressed up to look like a lead.
step3: WLED installed and connected. Under 3 minutes. Clean job.
flashSizeHint: Pick the flash size that fits your board - the chart above’s got the rundown on which chip families run which size.
layoutHint: Pick the board matching your HUB75 setup - the chart above’s got the chip and flash size it’s asking for.
memoryTypeHint: Only matters if your board’s carrying PSRAM - pick the option that fits its interface. Leave it on Standard if you’re not sure, or if your board’s carrying nothing at all.
flashModeHint: Default runs the flash mode this release’s standard build already carries for each chip - the safe bet, and the only way to stay square with an existing bootloader when you’re updating in place. DIO/QIO force the issue, where a matching build exists - check the chart above for which chips that’s good for.
